issues.description: coerceNumber silently changes behavior by mapping null/undefined to 0 instead of propagating NaN
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber as lift, which returns null for non-numeric input and produced NaN downstream. The new coerceNumber coerces null to 0, a runtime semantic change buried in a 'just types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or explicitly document the new postcondition.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the isNonEmpty guard runs
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) executes in panLog/zoomLog before delegating to pan/zoom, so an empty domain yields Math.sign(undefined) = NaN before the guard fires. The precondition check is in the wrong place. Hoist the non-empty check to each public entry point.

issues.description: Public Domain parameter type is number[] but the body requires NonEmptyArray<number>
issues.detail: Public signatures advertise number[] while the runtime guard asserts non-empty. The type system supports the stronger precondition via NonEmptyArray or readonly [number, ...number[]]; declaring it on the boundary makes the contract checkable at compile time rather than discovered at runtime. Half-typed is worse than fully typed.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw strengthens the public precondition without release-note documentation
issues.detail: The prior implementation soft-failed on empty domains (NaN/undefined arrays); the new implementation throws. This is a strengthened precondition at a published API boundary that breaks callers relying on the old behavior. Document the contract change in release notes and the type signature, or preserve backwards compatibility.

issues.description: Empty-domain tests cover only Linear; Log/Pow/Symlog entry points are unproved
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the same precondition but no test exercises them. Given the panLog/zoomLog sign-before-guard issue, the absent tests are especially material. Broaden the test matrix to cover all eight entry points.

issues.description: peek overload pair is sound but under-documented
issues.detail: The overloads form a sound ADT refinement: non-empty tuples guarantee T, generic arrays may yield undefined. However the contract is type-level only and may not survive noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Document the precondition in JSDoc so callers reading types understand why one overload returns T unconditionally.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR is a reasonable TypeScript port but smuggles two real behavior changes under a "types only" banner. First, coerceNumber replaces toNumber's null-propagation with a silent 0-coercion, changing observable output for non-numeric inputs. Second, empty-domain inputs now throw, strengthening a public precondition without documentation. The empty-domain guard is also misplaced in panLog/zoomLog (domain[0] is read before the check), and tests cover only the Linear path. The public Domain parameter type should be tightened to NonEmptyArray to move the contract into the type system. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge.
